title: Required parties and Rule 19
summary: Rule 19 asks whether an absent person should be joined and, if joinder is not feasible, whether the action can fairly proceed without that person. The inquiry protects existing parties, absentees, and the interest in complete resolution.
notes: Indispensable describes the conclusion that dismissal is required after analysis. Provident rejects using the label as a substitute for examining the actual interests and possible protection.

sections.Meaning: Rule 19 asks whether an absent person should be joined and, if joinder is not feasible, whether the action can fairly proceed without that person. The inquiry protects existing parties, absentees, and the interest in complete resolution.
sections.How to work through the question: First identify the need for the person’s participation under Rule 19(a). Then determine feasibility, including jurisdictional obstacles. If joinder is impossible, evaluate prejudice, ways to lessen it, adequacy of the judgment, and the consequences of dismissal under Rule 19(b).
